title: Enums and a first match
summary: An enum lists the possible shapes of a value; match handles each one by name.
lecture: An enum says a value is one of a fixed set of shapes: `enum Signal { Red, Green, Yellow }`. Variants can carry data: `Add(i32)`. You name variants through the type: `Signal::Red`.

`match` takes the value apart: each arm names a variant pattern, and a variant with data binds it - `Command::Add(n) => total + n`. Patterns must match the variant's shape exactly: matching `Add` without `(n)` is error E0532.
match must cover every variant (E0004 when it does not). That exhaustiveness is a feature: add a variant later and the compiler lists every match you must revisit.

example.caption: Each arm matches one shape; together they cover all of them.
